mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, indicating a sustained recovery from previous lows, will continue over the next four weeks, leading to higher average retail and recreation activity.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility continues its upward trend and surpasses -10% from baseline in the next week, it will signify a strong return to office, boosting weekday retail and recreation activity over the subsequent four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -10% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained recovery in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and daily routines, which will collectively drive increased retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their upward trends, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady state of easing restrictions, the decreasing trend in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with fluctuating but generally improving PARKS mobility indicates people are spending less time at home and more time outdoors, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation activity within the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decrease and PARKS remains positive, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent four-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a shift away from home-bound activities, directly correlating with an increase in out-of-home activities like retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility, after a slight dip, recovers and exceeds its t-1w peak of 9.9% in the next week, it will signal renewed general consumer confidence and activity, leading to a positive bump in RETAIL_REC within the next week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 9.9% but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not increase compared to the previous 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: As the weather improves (implied by PARKS mobility trending positive), increased outdoor activity (PARKS) will combine with the existing upward trend in RETAIL_REC, leading to an accelerated increase in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains positive, but RETAIL_REC does not show an accelerated increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of increasing economic activity, the inverse relationship between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility will strengthen; as WORKPLACES continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL falls, more people will be out and about, directly increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.
